ANCESTRY.value: CMA-ES (1996-, Hansen & Ostermeier): evolution strategy with covariance matrix adaptation and cumulative step-size adaptation; this is the author's own ANSI C code (cmaes.c), the ancestor of every pycma-style port

cut.note: the author's reference implementation: sample lambda points from N(m, sigma^2 C) via the eigen-decomposition C = B D^2 B'; rank the mu best; move the mean to their weighted average; accumulate two evolution paths (one whitened, for step size; one in C's coordinates, for covariance); adapt C by a rank-one term from the path and a rank-mu term from the selected steps; adapt sigma by comparing the whitened path's length with its expectation under random selection; the eigendecomposition is recomputed lazily; every constant has a default formula in N and mu_eff

organs.human_name: cmaes_SamplePopulation (608-658): x = m + sigma B (D z); cmaes_UpdateEigensystem (1881-1930): skip if up to date, if gen < last + modulo, or if eigen time exceeds 20 percent of total; the diagonal-only phase (diagonalCov iterations)
organs.mechanism: for each of lambda offspring draw z ~ N(0, I), scale by the eigenvalue square roots D, rotate by the eigenvectors B, scale by sigma and add the mean; the decomposition is recomputed only when flagged stale AND (a generation modulo has elapsed, default 1/(10 ccov N), OR when the eigen time is below 20 percent of the run's time); for the first diagonalCov generations (default 2 + 100 N / sqrt(lambda)) C is treated as diagonal and no decomposition happens; TestMinStdDevs inflates sigma until every coordinate's std exceeds a floor
assumptions: the O(N^3) decomposition can lag the O(N^2) covariance update by several generations without hurting progress; a diagonal start is cheaper and good enough early
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: the per-generation cost is O(N^2 lambda) except when the decomposition runs; the time cap makes the algorithm's overhead a bounded fraction
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: a stale decomposition samples from an outdated shape; the 20 percent rule is a wall-clock heuristic, so results differ between machines when it triggers
organs.human_prior: Hansen & Ostermeier 2001; the lazy update is the implementation's

organs.human_name: cmaes_UpdateDistribution (860-905): rgBDz = sqrt(mueff) (m_new - m_old)/sigma; rgdTmp = D^-1 B' rgBDz; ps = (1-cs) ps + sqrt(cs(2-cs)) B rgdTmp; hsig = ||ps|| / sqrt(1-(1-cs)^(2 gen)) / chiN < 1.4 + 2/(N+1); pc = (1-cc) pc + hsig sqrt(cc(2-cc)) rgBDz
organs.mechanism: the selected mean shift, scaled by sqrt(mu_eff)/sigma, is the per-generation evidence; the step-size path ps accumulates it after whitening (B D^-1 B') so that under random selection it is a standard normal vector of expected length chiN; the covariance path pc accumulates it unwhitened; hsig compares the normalised length of ps against a threshold and, when the path is too long (the mean is moving fast, typically early or after a jump), zeroes pc's update so the covariance does not learn a spurious direction; the initial-phase flag ends when ps's length statistic settles
assumptions: consecutive selected steps that point the same way are signal (the path grows); steps that cancel are noise (the path stays short); the whitened path's length under no selection is known, so it is a calibrated test statistic
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: step-size control without a success-rate rule; the covariance learns from correlations across generations, not only within one
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: the threshold constants (1.4 + 2/(N+1)) are tuned; the sqrt(1-(1-cs)^(2 gen)) bias correction matters only early; the flat-fitness escape multiplies sigma by exp(0.2 + cs/damps) with a warning
organs.human_prior: Hansen & Ostermeier 1996/2001 (cumulative step-size adaptation); Hansen 2016 tutorial for hsig

organs.human_name: Adapt_C2 (927-965): C = (1 - c1 - cmu) C + c1 (pc pc' + (1-hsig) cc(2-cc) C) + cmu sum_k w_k y_k y_k'; SupplementDefaults: lambda = 4 + 3 ln N, mu = lambda/2, cs = (mueff+2)/(N+mueff+3), cc = 4/(N+4), ccov from 2/(N+1.414)^2 and (2 mueff - 1)/((N+2)^2 + mueff), damps = 1 + 2 max(0, sqrt((mueff-1)/(N+1)) - 1) + cs
organs.mechanism: the lower triangle of C is blended: decayed by (1 - c1 - cmu), plus the outer product of the covariance path (with a variance-loss correction when hsig was zero), plus the weighted outer products of the mu selected steps (y_k = (x_k - m_old)/sigma); learning rates split a total ccov between the rank-one and rank-mu parts by 1/mucov; the decomposition is flagged stale; min/max diagonal are tracked for the termination tests; all constants come from formulas in N, mu_eff and lambda unless a parameter file overrides them
assumptions: the selected steps' second moment, accumulated with a slow learning rate, estimates a covariance under which the successful steps become isotropic (the CMA principle); the defaults are the ones the literature validated
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: invariance under rotations and rescaling of the problem; ill-conditioned problems solved without derivative information
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: O(N^2) memory and O(N^3) decomposition bound N to a few hundred; the flat-fitness and TolUpX warnings are the implementation's own failure detectors

organs.mechanism: sigma grows when the whitened path is longer than a random walk's expected length chiN (selected steps are correlated: the step is too small) and shrinks when shorter (steps cancel: too large); the exponent is scaled by cs/damps, damps defaulting to about 1 + cs for large N
assumptions: path length is a scale-free, rotation-invariant signal of step-size adequacy
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: log-linear convergence on the sphere at a rate independent of the initial sigma
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: in a dynamic environment the path's momentum is 'harmful' (the author's own #if 0 comment on the removed momentum fix)
organs.source_boundary: one line plus the path organ

organs.human_name: cmaes_TestForTermination (1531-1640): Fitness, TolFun (range over history and current), TolFunHist, TolX (sigma sqrt(C_ii) and sigma pc_i all below), TolUpX (sigma grew by a factor over the initial stds), ConditionNumber (maxEW >= minEW 1e14), NoEffectAxis (m unchanged by 0.1 sigma along an eigenvector), NoEffectCoord (m unchanged by 0.2 sigma along a coordinate), MaxFunEvals, MaxIter, Manual
organs.mechanism: each criterion is tested independently and, if met, appends a human-readable line with the measured value to a shared string; the caller reads the string as 'stop' and the reasons; the two NoEffect tests probe floating-point resolution directly (x == x + fac * step) rather than a tolerance, and TolUpX detects divergence rather than convergence
assumptions: different failure modes need different detectors; a stop must say why so the user can restart with a changed setting (the restart strategies in example_restarts.c consume these reasons)
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: the algorithm reports its own inapplicability (divergence, numerical exhaustion, flat fitness) instead of looping
organs.human_prior: Hansen's termination criteria as listed in the tutorial

pressures.source_evidence: cmaes.c UpdateDistribution, Adapt_C2, TestForTermination; the diagonalCov and parameter-file switches
pressures.condition: an organism sees only the ranking of lambda evaluated points per generation; the objective's Hessian is unknown, ill-conditioned and rotated; the budget is function evaluations; the score is evaluations to a target precision across a suite
pressures.resource_or_constraint: lambda evaluations per generation; O(N^2) memory
pressures.failure_condition: evaluations growing with the condition number (an isotropic search), or premature convergence from step-size collapse, or divergence
pressures.world_punishes: fixed step sizes; diagonal-only covariance on rotated problems; success-rule step control on noisy rankings
pressures.world_rewards: a covariance that whitens the selected steps; path-length step control; calibrated stopping
pressures.observable_consequence: evaluations to target vs condition number on rotated ellipsoids, for the full update vs diagonal-only (the body's own diagonalCov switch) vs rank-one only (cmu = 0) vs no step-size adaptation (cs = 0)
pressures.cheat_control: an organism given the Hessian must reach the target in evaluations independent of the condition number (the bound); the diagonal-only organism must show evaluations growing with the condition number on rotated ellipsoids and not on axis-aligned ones; cs = 0 must stall or diverge: the world must show all three
